messages:
ci-bot: PERF ALERT: nightly/ci-perf/kernel-select job exceeded latency SLO. 99p latency +38% vs baseline. job: ci/perf/kernel-select-99p. link: https://ci.example/redwood/12345
felix: saw the spike on the infra dashboard too. timeline aligns with merge of PR 0f4b2c (batching heuristics). suspect kernel selector fallback to generic_cuda for long sequences.
maya: starting a bisect on main between tags v1.12.0..HEAD to narrow down the commit. running: `python contrib/bench/bisect_perf.py --metric=latency_99 --threshold=+25%`
samir: quick local profile: ~2x more kernel switches for long-seq workloads after that merge; KV cache hit rate looks stable. I'll attach a flamegraph shortly.
ana_typo_fix: (ignore)
ana: attaching flamegraph: /tmp/flame-1825.svg. nvprof snapshot points to kernel selection heuristics. suspicious commit is `d3a9b7f` in pkg/runtime/kernel_chooser.cc — changes scoring weights.
felix: can we cherry-pick `d3a9b7f` to `release/v1.12` as a hotfix? looks small and targeted to kernel scoring.
maya: creating branch `hotfix/kernel-score-backport` and will cherry-pick `d3a9b7f`. plan: open PR -> run perf CI -> canary deploy on dedicated pool. tagging @samir @ana for reviews.
samir: good plan. after cherry-pick run: `bench/runner --config=ci/perf/config.yml --workload=kernel-select --runs=5` and compare latency_99. also add `--kv-cache-heat=warm` to match production distribution.
jordan: QA checklist: canary on dedicated pool (5 nodes) with 50% traffic for 1h, run synthetic workload (seq_len distribution attached) and smoke test for 1-token latency. I'll coordinate infra.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: hotfix/kernel-score-backport -> release/v1.12; canary: 5 nodes, start=2026-03-19T16:30:00Z
maya: PR opened: https://git.example/redwood/runtime/pulls/6789. CI artifacts include perf runs and flamegraphs. requesting review from @samir @ana.
samir: reviewing now. quick diff looks fine. main risk is unintentionally favoring an older kernel on short sequences — will validate.
felix: note to reviewers: keep an eye on batching windows; if we see tail latency regress on 1-token requests revert the backport and investigate batching heuristic interaction.
ana_correction: (sorry typo earlier; that was me) local perf numbers after applying the cherry-pick: baseline 99p=120ms -> patched 99p=126ms (was 165ms on main).
maya: merged after approvals and green perf CI. kicking off canary. :eyes:
deploy-bot: canary report @60m: no regression detected vs baseline on latency_99, error rates normal. proceeding to rollout to full release. :shipit:
felix: thanks everyone. follow-up action: add unit test for kernel scoring and a small integration perf check to CI to catch this class of regressions going forward.
